what_it_is: AI security platform with firewall, red teaming, model and agent scanning.
identity_note: "DeepLeep" resolved to DeepKeep (deepkeep.ai), an Israeli AI security platform. No AI security vendor named DeepLeep exists.

1.reason: AI Lens finds shadow AI use. Model Scanning covers the model supply chain. No cloud AI inventory.
1.evidence: Shine a light on shadow AI
1.verify_note: AI Lens page confirms shadow AI discovery of AI services (usage view, so 1.1 partial). Model Scanning covers supply chain, 1.3 partial.

2.reason: AI Agent Scanner maps agent tools and risks. MCP servers get allow or block decisions.
2.evidence: We identify which MCP servers are being used, recommend whether to allow or block them
2.verify_note: Use-case page confirms MCP allow or block. Platform list (Agentforce, Bedrock AgentCore, Microsoft) comes from SiliconANGLE 3 Mar 2026, a third-party source, so 2.1 yes rests on press.

3.reason: AI Firewall inspects live traffic and blocks or redacts. No SIEM, SOAR or ticketing integration found.
3.evidence: If something violates your standards, we block or redact it before it causes harm. Otherwise, we alert you.
3.verify_note: Firewall page confirms block or redact. rfp.wiki says DeepKeep integrates with SIEMs and XDRs but names none, so 3.2 moves to partial.

4.reason: AI Firewall runs 60+ guardrails for injection, PII, toxicity and hallucination. Plugs into TrueFoundry AI Gateway.
4.evidence: Safeguards against data leakage, protecting sensitive data and personal data or PII
4.verify_note: LLM page confirms injection, PII, toxicity and hallucination coverage. Home page lists 60+ runtime guardrails.

5.reason: Model Scanning produces an MLBOM and firewall events are logged. Named framework mapping is not shown.
5.evidence: roll up into a single risk posture - mapped to the frameworks your auditors already use
5.verify_note: Home page mapping line names no framework, so 5.2 drops to partial. Firewall page says everything is logged and auditable, so 5.3 rises to yes. Status unchanged.

6.reason: AI Red Teaming tests apps, agents and models. The Vibe red teaming agent adapts attacks live.
6.evidence: prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage attempts, and unsafe output generation. Tests run contextually and continuously
6.verify_note: Red teaming page confirms apps, agents, models, continuous runs and the Reddy red teaming agent.

7.reason: AI Lens ties AI tool access to IdP user roles. No agent identity or NHI governance found.
7.evidence: By integrating with your existing Identity Provider (IdP), AI Lens allows you to manage access to AI tools by user roles.
7.verify_note: AI Lens confirms IdP role-based access to AI tools. Search for agent identity found nothing.

8.reason: Model Scanning checks model files for malware and tampering. No dataset scanner or AI SAST found.
8.evidence: Detect embedded malware, known vulnerabilities in model dependencies, signs of tampering
8.verify_note: Model Scanning page confirms malware and tamper detection. Blog mentions PII scanning of fine-tuning data and vision page covers dataset integrity, so 8.2 stays partial.

notes: Docs at docs.deepkeep.ai are password protected, so claims rest on product pages and press. AI Agent Scanner launched March 2026 (SiliconANGLE, 3 Mar 2026) with runtime protection for select frameworks: Microsoft, Agentforce, OpenAI Agents, CrewAI, Bedrock AgentCore, n8n, Make. SiliconANGLE said an agent red teaming product was forthcoming at that time. Also sells DeepKeep for Vision. The LLM page lists poisoning as a threat, but no dataset scanning product. Press and blog page bodies did not render in scrapes. Two searches for SIEM or SOAR integration and two for agent identity found nothing.
